definition_en: the red liquid that flows through the body
core_image: 验血时试管里的暗红色液体
scene: 护士把试管举到灯下。A drop of blood fell onto the white cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 blood 是「血」（第 1 个义项：在体内流动的红色液体）；句意是一滴血落在白布上。

senses.title: The red liquid of the body
senses.definition: the red liquid that carries oxygen through the body
senses.definitionCN: 在体内输送氧气的红色液体
senses.example: A drop of blood fell onto the white cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴血落在白布上。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the physical liquid itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指实实在在的液体。

senses.title: Family origin
senses.definition: the family line a person comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所出自的家族血脉
senses.example: She has royal blood in her family.
senses.exampleCN: 她的家族有王室血统。
senses.why: Kinship was thought to run in the blood, so the liquid named the line.
senses.whyCN: 人们认为亲属关系随血而流，于是这液体成了血统的代称。

senses.title: Strong feeling
senses.definition: powerful emotion, especially anger
senses.definitionCN: 强烈的情绪，尤其是愤怒
senses.example: The unfair decision made his blood boil.
senses.exampleCN: 那个不公平的决定让他怒火中烧。
senses.why: Emotion was felt as heat moving through the blood.
senses.whyCN: 情绪被感受为在血液里流动的热度。

intro.en: Blood is an old Germanic word for the liquid of life.
intro.cn: blood 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，指生命之液。

items.cn: blod 指生命所系的红色液体。

items.en: blood also meant family line.
items.cn: blood 也开始指家族血统。

items.en: blood stood for strong feeling in phrases.
items.cn: 在固定说法里，blood 表示强烈的情绪。

items.en: blood tests became a medical tool.
items.cn: 验血成为医学手段。

items.en: blood covers liquid, lineage and passion.
items.cn: 如今 blood 兼指血液、血统与激情。

normal.cn: blood 不可数，没有复数形式。

normal.cn: blood pressure 是常见医学说法。

normal.en: In cold blood means without pity.
normal.cn: in cold blood 表示冷酷无情地。

normal.en: Blood relation means a family tie.
normal.cn: blood relation 指血缘关系。

definition_en: to send out air from the mouth, or to move air
core_image: 对着蒲公英吹散绒毛
scene: 她捏着蒲公英，轻轻吹了一口气。Blow out the candles on the cake.
sceneCN: 这里 blow 是「吹」（第 1 个义项：用力送出气流）；句意是吹灭蛋糕上的蜡烛。

senses.title: To send out a stream of air
senses.definition: to push air out of the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 把气流从口中送出
senses.example: Blow out the candles on the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 吹灭蛋糕上的蜡烛。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the breath itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，就是呼出的那口气。

senses.title: To move something with air
senses.definition: to move or carry something by moving air
senses.definitionCN: 借流动的空气使某物移动
senses.example: The wind blew the leaves across the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 风把树叶吹过院子。
senses.why: A breath grew into wind, and wind moves what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 一口气扩展成风，风会推动它碰到的东西。

senses.title: A hard hit or a shock
senses.definition: a hard strike, or a sudden shock
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈的一击，或突然的打击
senses.example: Losing the job was a heavy blow.
senses.exampleCN: 失去那份工作是一次沉重打击。
senses.why: A stroke of air became a stroke of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 一股气流的冲击，变成了手上的一击。

senses.title: To burst or explode
senses.definition: to break open or explode
senses.definitionCN: 裂开或炸开
senses.example: The tank blew up at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 水箱在中午炸开了。
senses.why: The phrase blow up first meant to inflate, then to burst.
senses.whyCN: blow up 先表示充气，后来表示炸开。

senses.title: Of the colour of a clear sky

senses.example: The lake turned deep blue at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时湖水变成深蓝色。

senses.title: A long thin piece of wood

definition_en: the whole physical structure of a person or animal

senses.title: The physical form of a person
senses.definition: the whole physical structure of a person or animal

senses.title: The main part

definition_en: to heat a liquid until it bubbles
core_image: 锅底不断冒起的水泡
scene: 锅里的水过了几分钟开始翻滚。The water began to boil after a few minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 boil 是「沸腾」（第 1 个义项：液体受热冒出气泡）；句意是几分钟后水开始沸腾。

senses.title: To bubble with heat
senses.definition: to heat a liquid until it bubbles and gives off steam
senses.definitionCN: 把液体加热到冒泡并冒出蒸汽
senses.example: The water began to boil after a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 几分钟后水开始沸腾。
senses.why: This is the core sense, taken from the Latin word for a bubble.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自拉丁语中表示气泡的词。

senses.title: To cook in hot water
senses.definition: to cook food in water that is boiling
senses.definitionCN: 在沸腾的水中烹煮食物
senses.example: She boiled two eggs for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早饭煮了两个鸡蛋。
senses.why: Cooking in bubbling water is the everyday use of the same action.
senses.whyCN: 在冒泡的水里烹煮，是这一动作最常见的用法。

senses.title: To be very angry
senses.definition: to feel extremely angry, as if heat were rising
senses.definitionCN: 极度愤怒，像热气往上冲
senses.example: He was boiling with anger after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会后他怒火中烧。
senses.why: Anger is pictured as heat, so the bubbling of water became a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被比作高温，水的翻滚便引申为情绪。

intro.en: Boil goes back through French to Latin bulla, a bubble.

items.en: bulla meant a bubble or a round object.
items.cn: bulla 指气泡或圆形之物。

definition_en: a tank or device that heats water or makes steam, often for heating a building
core_image: 地下室里轰隆作响、烧着热水的大铁罐
scene: 冬天来临前，工人下到地下室检查那只轰隆作响的大铁罐。The old boiler in the basement finally broke down last night.
sceneCN: 这里 boiler 是「锅炉」（第 1 个义项：烧水供热的设备）；句意是地下室里那台旧锅炉昨晚终于坏了。

senses.title: A device that heats water
senses.definition: a closed tank that heats water or produces steam for heating or power
senses.definitionCN: 加热水或产生蒸汽、用于供暖或提供动力的密闭容器
senses.example: The old boiler in the basement finally broke down last night.
senses.exampleCN: 地下室里那台旧锅炉昨晚终于坏了。
senses.why: The -er suffix names a tool by the action it performs, so a boiler is the thing that boils.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 用动作来命名工具，boiler 就是「用来煮水的东西」。

senses.title: A vessel for boiling food or liquid
senses.definition: a pot or container used for boiling things, such as a fish kettle
senses.definitionCN: 用来煮东西的锅或容器，如煮鱼的长锅
senses.example: She put the ham into a large boiler and let it simmer for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她把火腿放进一口大煮锅里，小火煨了好几个小时。
senses.why: The same tool-naming logic extends to everyday cookware that boils food.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「以动作命名工具」逻辑延伸到了日常煮食的锅具。

senses.title: A very hot room or situation
senses.definition: informally, a hot, stuffy place that feels like being boiled
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指热得像被蒸煮一样的闷热地方
senses.example: Without air conditioning, the dorm turned into a boiler in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 没有空调，夏天宿舍闷热得像个蒸笼。
senses.why: The heat of a boiler becomes a vivid image for any stiflingly hot place.
senses.whyCN: 锅炉的高温被拿来比喻任何闷热难耐的场所。

sceneCN: 这里 boot 是「靴子」（第 1 个义项：包住脚踝和小腿的鞋）；句意是门口放着一双沾泥的靴子。

senses.title: A shoe that covers the ankle
senses.definition: a strong shoe covering the ankle and sometimes the leg
senses.definitionCN: 包住脚踝、有时包到小腿的结实鞋子
senses.example: A pair of muddy boots stood by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门口放着一双沾泥的靴子。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from a French word for a heavy shoe.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自法语中表示厚鞋的词。

senses.title: The luggage space of a car
senses.definition: the covered space at the back of a car for bags
senses.definitionCN: 汽车后部放行李的有盖空间
senses.example: Put the bags in the boot of the car.
senses.exampleCN: 把包放到汽车后备箱里。
senses.why: An old coach had a boot-shaped box for luggage at the back.
senses.whyCN: 旧式马车后部有个靴形的箱子放行李。

senses.title: To start a computer
senses.definition: to make a computer start working
senses.definitionCN: 让计算机开始运行
senses.example: The computer takes a minute to boot.
senses.exampleCN: 这台电脑启动需要一分钟。
senses.why: Starting a machine was compared to pulling yourself up by your bootstraps.
senses.whyCN: 启动机器被比作拉着自己的靴带站起来。

definition_en: the line that divides two countries

scene: 两国的界碑立在山口。They crossed the border at a small mountain pass.

senses.title: A line between countries
senses.definition: the line that separates two countries

senses.example: They crossed the border at a small mountain pass.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一个小山口越过边界。
senses.why: This is the strongest modern sense, from a word for an edge.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常用的义项，来自表示边缘的词。

senses.title: The outer edge

definition_zh: 使厌烦；钻孔；令人厌烦的人
definition_en: to make someone feel tired and uninterested
core_image: 听众在长讲座上打哈欠
scene: 那场讲座又长又闷，让人昏昏欲睡。The long lecture bored the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里 bore 是「使厌烦」（第 1 个义项：让人感到无聊、提不起兴趣）；句意是那场长讲座让全班都感到乏味。

pos.zh: 名词：令人厌烦的人或事

senses.title: To make someone tired
senses.definition: to make someone feel tired because nothing interests them
senses.definitionCN: 因为毫无趣味而让人感到疲惫
senses.example: The long lecture bored the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 那场长讲座让全班都感到乏味。
senses.why: This is the everyday modern sense, though it came later than drilling.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代日常义项，但出现得比钻孔晚。

senses.title: To make a hole
senses.definition: to make a deep round hole in something
senses.definitionCN: 在某物上钻出深的圆孔
senses.example: They bored a hole through the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在墙上钻了一个洞。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from an Old English word for piercing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自古英语中表示穿刺的词。

senses.title: A dull person
senses.definition: a person who makes others feel tired and uninterested
senses.definitionCN: 让别人觉得无聊、提不起兴趣的人
senses.example: He is a bore at parties.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上是个乏味的人。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the person who causes the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，指引起这种感觉的人。

intro.en: Bore first meant to pierce; the sense of being dull is much later.

definition_en: brought into life at birth

sceneCN: 这里 born 是「出生」（第 1 个义项：从母体中诞生）；句意是她出生在一个海边小镇。

pos.zh: 动词：bear 的过去分词，意为出生

senses.title: Brought into life
senses.definition: coming into life from the body of a mother

senses.example: She was born in a small town by the sea.

core_image: 向邻居借来的一把梯子
scene: 他向邻居借了一把梯子。He borrowed a ladder from his neighbour.
sceneCN: 这里 borrow 是「借入」（第 1 个义项：从别人那里暂时取得，之后归还）；句意是他向邻居借了一把梯子。

senses.title: To take and return later
senses.definition: to take something from someone and give it back later
senses.definitionCN: 从别人那里取来，之后再归还
senses.example: He borrowed a ladder from his neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 他向邻居借了一把梯子。

senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自古英语中表示抵押的词。

senses.title: To use something temporarily
senses.definition: to use something that belongs to someone else for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 短时间使用属于别人的东西

senses.exampleCN: 我可以借用你的笔吗？

senses.title: To adopt a word or idea

normal.cn: 从图书馆借一本书。

normal.en: A borrower must return what was taken.
normal.cn: 借的人必须归还所借之物。

normal.en: English borrowed words from many languages.
normal.cn: 英语从许多语言中借词。

abstract.en: See a ladder carried home and brought back.
abstract.cn: 想象把梯子扛回家，用完再送回去。

abstract.en: See a pen passed across a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔从桌子那头递过来。

abstract.en: See a French word moving into an English page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法语词挪进英文书页。

examples.en: He borrowed a ladder from his neighbour.
examples.cn: 他向邻居借了一把梯子。

examples.en: May I borrow your pen?
examples.cn: 我可以借用你的笔吗？

examples.en: English borrowed many words from French.
examples.cn: 英语借用了许多法语词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 bor 想成「抱」，row 想成「搂」：抱过来、搂一下，用完再还，就是借入。

root: borrow 源自古英语 borgian，本指以抵押方式取得，中古英语指暂时取得钱物，十四世纪起也用于借用词语与观念。

sensesIntro.en: Taking something to return, using it briefly, and adopting words or ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 取来要归还的东西、短暂使用，以及借用词语或观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ladder carried home and later returned.
core.cn: 核心意象：借回家、之后再归还的梯子。

intro.en: Borrow takes -er and -ing, and pairs with loan and lend.
intro.cn: borrow 可加 -er 与 -ing，并与 loan、lend 搭配。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old English; the items below are related in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语，下面的词只在意思上相关。

items.meaning: to give something for a time
to take and use as your own

definition_zh: 老板；上司；发号施令；头目
definition_en: the person in charge of a group of workers
core_image: 站在办公室门口点名的上司
scene: 新来的经理把大家叫进会议室。Our boss called a meeting on Monday morning.
sceneCN: 这里 boss 是「老板；上司」（第 1 个义项：负责管理员工的人）；句意是老板周一早上召集了会议。

senses.title: A person in charge
senses.definition: the person who manages workers and gives them orders
senses.definitionCN: 管理员工并给他们下指令的人
senses.example: Our boss called a meeting on Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 老板周一早上召集了会议。
senses.why: This is the main sense, from a Dutch word for master.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要义项，来自荷兰语中表示主人的词。

senses.title: To give orders
senses.definition: to tell people what to do, often rudely
senses.definitionCN: 常指粗鲁地指使别人做事
senses.example: She hates being bossed around.
senses.exampleCN: 她讨厌被人呼来喝去。
senses.why: To act like the boss became a verb for giving orders.
senses.whyCN: 表现得像老板一样，便转化为下命令的动词。

senses.title: A leader of a group
senses.definition: the leader of a group, especially a criminal one
senses.definitionCN: 某个团体的首领，尤指犯罪团伙
senses.example: He was the boss of a small gang.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一个小团伙的头目。
senses.why: The idea of the one in charge spread from work to any group.
senses.whyCN: 「说了算的人」这一概念从职场扩展到任何团体。

intro.en: Boss comes from Dutch baas, a word for a master, and crossed into American English.
intro.cn: boss 来自荷兰语 baas，指主人，后进入美国英语。

items.en: baas meant a master or an uncle.
items.cn: baas 指主人或大叔。

items.en: boss entered American English for a master.
items.cn: boss 以主人之义进入美国英语。

items.en: boss around meant to give rude orders.
items.cn: boss around 指粗鲁地差遣别人。

items.en: boss spread to every kind of workplace.
items.cn: boss 扩展到各类工作场所。

items.en: boss means a manager or any leader.
items.cn: 如今 boss 指上司或任何首领。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes with boss; the near-meaning group names people in charge.
note.cn: 形近组与 boss 押韵；近义组是负责管理的人。

entries.definition: a small green plant on damp surfaces
a person who controls part of a business
a person who pays others to work

normalIntro.en: Boss is the one whose name goes first on the office door.
normalIntro.cn: boss 就是名字写在办公室门上第一个人的人。

normal.en: Boss and bosses are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 boss，复数是 bosses。

normal.en: The boss decides who does what.
normal.cn: 老板决定谁做什么。

normal.en: Bossy people love to give orders.
normal.cn: 爱发号施令的人总是想指挥别人。

normal.en: To boss someone around is to treat them rudely.
normal.cn: boss someone around 指粗鲁地差遣别人。

normal.en: A gang boss leads a criminal group.
normal.cn: 团伙头目领导一个犯罪集团。

abstract.en: See a name plate on a closed office door.
abstract.cn: 想象关着的办公室门上的名牌。

abstract.en: See a hand pointing at a duty list.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指着任务清单。

abstract.en: See a group waiting for one man to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人等一个人开口。

examples.en: Our boss called a meeting on Monday morning.
examples.cn: 老板周一早上召集了会议。

examples.en: She hates being bossed around.
examples.cn: 她讨厌被人呼来喝去。

examples.en: He was the boss of a small gang.
examples.cn: 他是一个小团伙的头目。

dict_mnemonic.text: boss 读起来像「博士」的去声：办公室里最有学问、说了算的人，就是老板。

root: boss 来自荷兰语 baas（主人、大叔），十七世纪进入美国英语指雇主，十九世纪产生「差遣」的动词用法，再引申为任何团体的头目。

sensesIntro.en: The person in charge, the act of ordering people, and the leader of any group.
sensesIntro.cn: 管事的人、指使别人的行为，以及任何团体的首领。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name plate on the manager's door.
core.cn: 核心意象：经理办公室门上的名牌。

intro.en: Boss takes -y and -ness to name a manner and its quality.
intro.cn: boss 加 -y 与 -ness 可表示作风及其性质。

latinIntro.en: The base is Dutch; the items below share the idea of authority.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自荷兰语，下面的词都围绕权威。

definition_en: the two together, not just one of them
core_image: 两只手同时举起
scene: 两个孩子都通过了考试。Both children passed the exam.
sceneCN: 这里 both 是「两者都」（第 1 个义项：指两个人或物一起）；句意是两个孩子都通过了考试。

derivatives.zh: 语义关联词，义为两者之一
语义关联词，义为两者都不

senses.title: The two together
senses.definition: the two people or things, not only one
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或物一起，而不只是其中一个
senses.example: Both children passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 两个孩子都通过了考试。
senses.why: This is the central sense, naming two things as a pair.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，把两个事物作为一个整体来说。

senses.title: One and the other
senses.definition: used with and to join two qualities or actions
senses.definitionCN: 与 and 连用，连接两种性质或动作
senses.example: The plan is both cheap and quick.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划既便宜又快捷。
senses.why: The same word links two qualities that are true at once.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词用来连接同时成立的两个特点。

intro.en: Both comes from an Old Norse word for the two together.
intro.cn: both 来自古诺尔斯语中表示「两者一起」的词。

items.en: bathir meant the two together.
items.cn: bathir 意为两者一起。

items.en: both named two things as a pair.
items.cn: both 把两个事物作为一个对子。

items.en: both and joined two qualities.
items.cn: both and 用来连接两种性质。

items.en: both of them became a common phrase.
items.cn: both of them 成为常见说法。

items.en: both names two together and joins two qualities.
items.cn: 如今 both 既指两者一起，也连接两种性质。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names one of two or neither.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组指两者之一或两者都不。

entries.definition: a large container for washing the body
a small closed place for one person
one or the other of two
not one and not the other

normalIntro.en: Both means the pair, never just one half of it.
normalIntro.cn: both 指的是整个一对，从不是其中一半。

normal.en: Both never changes its form.
normal.cn: both 没有词形变化。

normal.en: Both of them agreed.
normal.cn: 他们两个人都同意了。

normal.en: Both sides of the road were full.
normal.cn: 路的两边都满了。

normal.en: Both and joins two qualities.
normal.cn: both and 连接两种性质。

normal.en: He held the cup in both hands.
normal.cn: 他用双手捧着杯子。

abstract.en: See two hands going up at once.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手同时举起。

abstract.en: See two doors opening together.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门一起打开。

abstract.en: See a scale with two equal pans.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端一般重。

examples.en: Both children passed the exam.
examples.cn: 两个孩子都通过了考试。

examples.en: She held the cup in both hands.
examples.cn: 她用双手捧着杯子。

examples.en: The plan is both cheap and quick.
examples.cn: 这个计划既便宜又快捷。

dict_mnemonic.text: both 里的 b 和 o 像两个并排的圆圈，两个圈都算上，就是「两者都」。

root: both 源自古诺尔斯语 bathir，本义就是「两者一起」，中古英语进入英语后，又发展出 both and 连接两种性质的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Two things taken together, and two qualities held at the same time.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个事物一起，以及同时成立的两种性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands raised at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：同时举起的两只手。

intro.en: Both has no endings; it pairs with either and neither.
intro.cn: both 没有词尾变化，常与 either、neither 对照。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old Norse; the items below share the idea of two.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古诺尔斯语，下面的词都围绕「二」。

items.meaning: one or the other of two
not one and not the other
one of two children born together
